name: New York State Pavilion
features: Elliptical 'Tent of Tomorrow' with a cable-suspended roof on concrete columns, beside the observation towers.

photos.file: File:Flushing Meadows Fair Grounds td (2018-05-26) 040 - New York State Pavilion.jpg
File:1965 World's Fair- New York State Pavilion.jpg

note: Built for the 1964 World's Fair; the Tent of Tomorrow's files sit in Category:Tent of Tomorrow. Third photo is a 1965 view.

name: No 1 Poultry
by: James Stirling, Michael Wilford and Associates
features: Wedge-shaped block in bands of pink and yellow stone, with a clock and turret on its sharp prow.

photos.file: File:1 Poultry, London from Bank junction.jpg
File:View of 1 Poultry from Queen Victoria Street - geograph.org.uk - 4330680.jpg

note: Completed after Stirling's death (1992). Grade II* listed.

name: The Pyramids (College Life Insurance)
by: Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates
features: Three 11-storey pyramids: blank concrete walls face the highway, sloping glass walls face the lake.
note: Second photo is black and white.

name: Dallas City Hall
features: Concrete wedge whose front leans out over the plaza, each floor projecting beyond the one below.

photos.file: File:Ground level view of main elevation looking southeast - Dallas City Hall, City Hall Plaza, Dallas, Dallas County, TX HABS TEX,57-DAL,1-4.tif

note: Category also holds public-domain HABS survey photos (aerial and ground views).

name: Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art (MACBA)
features: White panelled block with a glazed ramp hall along the square and a curved drum lifted on columns.
commons_category: Category:Exterior of the Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona

photos.file: File:Barcelona - Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona (MACBA).jpg
File:Museum of Contemporary Art of Barcelona - Barcelona 2014 (2).JPG

name: Bensberg Town Hall
features: Concrete town hall built into a medieval castle's ruins, crowned by a jagged stair tower.
note: Böhm's Wikipedia works list gives 1962–69. Many more photos in the category, several public domain.

name: Mondadori Palace
features: Five-storey glass office block hung from concrete arches of differing widths, floating over a lake.

photos.file: File:Mondadori headquarters by Oscar Niemeyer, Segrate (Milano) 07.jpg
File:Mondadori headquarters by Oscar Niemeyer, Segrate (Milano) 01.jpg
File:Mondadori headquarters by Oscar Niemeyer, Segrate (Milano) 05.jpg

note: Italy has no freedom of panorama and Niemeyer died in 2012, so these 2019-era CC BY-SA photos may be at risk of deletion on Commons; worth keeping an eye on. Third photo shows the curved low annex.

name: Kagawa Prefectural Gymnasium
features: Concrete roof shaped like a ship's hull, raised on massive end piers over a glass-walled hall.
note: Known as the 'ship gym'. Closed since 2014; the prefecture began a demolition tender in August 2025 and campaigners sought an injunction, so it may be demolished. No Commons category; second photo is an old black-and-white view. File:香川県体育館.jpg (1129px) is credited to the builder, so I left it out.

name: Ray and Maria Stata Center (MIT Building 32)
features: Leaning towers in brick, steel and coloured panels, crowded together like a small hill town.

name: Quartier Schützenstraße
features: One city block split into many narrow, brightly coloured facades around inner courtyards.
note: Rossi's Wikipedia works list gives 1994–1998. Offices, flats and shops. Rossi died in 1997, before completion.

name: Franklin Court
by: Venturi and Rauch (Robert Venturi, Denise Scott Brown)
features: White steel 'ghost' frames trace Franklin's vanished house and print shop above an underground museum.

photos.file: File:The large white steel frame in the foreground marks the location and size of Benjamin Franklin's home in Franklin Court (3d00c6b9-155d-451f-67cb-cdfa110dc69e).jpg
File:Independence National Historical Park Franklin Court Ghost Structure.jpg

note: Fourth photo is a black-and-white aerial view. Also an aerial 1980 photo (public domain) with a printed caption under it.

name: Galician Centre of Contemporary Art (CGAC)
features: Granite-clad wedges beside a convent, with a deep cut-away entrance porch and a roof terrace over the old town.
commons_category: Category:Exterior of the Centro Galego de Arte Contemporánea
note: Wikipedia: designed from 1988, built 1993–94, opened 1993.

name: LVMH Tower
features: 24-storey tower of folded, faceted glass on 57th Street, set against its masonry neighbours.

name: Hill of the Buddha
features: A 13.5 m Buddha ringed by a lavender-planted hill; only its head shows until you enter by a tunnel.

photos.file: File:Hill of the Buddha, Makomanai Takino Cemetery 1 - Jul 11, 2020.jpg

note: Only one exterior photo (entrance and water court with the hill behind). File:頭大仏（2024）.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0) shows the Buddha inside the open rotunda, a good second image if interiors are allowed.

name: Murcia Town Hall Extension
features: Sandstone facade of irregular piers and openings, like a musical score, facing the cathedral square.
note: Built 1991–98 (Moneo's site, archINFORM). No door onto the square; entered from the side.

name: Ivar Aasen Centre (Ivar Aasen-tunet)
features: Low museum dug into the hillside, marked by tall sloping concrete wedges rising from the slope.
note: Second and third photos are distant views across the meadow; the first is a close-up of one concrete wedge.

name: Kansai International Airport Terminal 1
features: 1.7 km terminal under one curved, wing-like steel roof, on an artificial island in Osaka Bay.

photos.file: File:関空第1ターミナル全景 - panoramio.jpg
File:Kansai Airport terminal 1 ,from the top of observation hall "sky view" (16041786233).jpg

note: Photos are airside views with aircraft in front.

name: Zentrum Paul Klee
features: Three steel-ribbed waves rising out of the fields, for galleries, archive and a children's studio.
note: The best exterior photos are found by file search, not in the category itself (which is mostly 2017 garden shots).

name: Hong Kong International Airport Terminal 1
features: Vast terminal under a repeated run of light steel barrel-vaulted roof shells that let daylight in.
note: Third photo is an aerial view from a plane.

name: Apple Park
features: Four-storey ring of curved glass with white floor canopies, around a planted central courtyard.
note: Private campus: most public views are from the street through trees. Third photo shows it under construction.

name: Milstein Hall, Cornell University
features: Long glass studio floor that cantilevers over the street, linking two old architecture buildings.

photos.file: File:Milstein and Sibley Halls, Cornell University.jpg

note: Below the studio floor: a stepped auditorium and sunken garden (Wikipedia).

name: Prada Aoyama
features: Crystal-like shop wrapped in a diamond grid of glass panes, some bulging out, some curving in.
note: A flagship shop; typed as Workplace, as for Maison Hermès.

name: Fredensborg Houses
features: Courtyard houses strung along a slope, each with a walled garden, all facing a shared meadow.
note: Built for Danes who had worked long abroad (Wikipedia). Completion year 1963 not in the Wikipedia intro; it is the commonly published date, please double-check.

name: Pierresvives
features: Long horizontal 'tree trunk' of concrete and glass holding the archives, library and sports offices.
note: Only one usable photo. France has no freedom of panorama for recent buildings: the other file in the category (Pierres vives Montpellier 03B.jpg) has the building blacked out, and this one could be deleted. If it goes, this is a good candidate to draw.

name: European Court of Human Rights Building
by: Richard Rogers Partnership with Claude Bucher
features: Two drum-shaped courtrooms at the head of a long office 'tail', on the bank of the river Ill.

photos.file: File:Cour européenne des droits de l'homme (Strasbourg) (2).jpg
File:Cour européenne des droits de l'homme (Strasbourg) (1).jpg

note: In France (no freedom of panorama; Rogers died 2021), so these photos could be removed from Commons later. The category is about the court as an institution; the building photos are mixed in with portraits and documents.

name: Lucerne Culture and Congress Centre (KKL)
features: A thin 100 m square roof cantilevers far out over the lakeside, sheltering concert hall, museum and congress halls.

photos.file: File:KKL Luzern. Kultur- und Kongresszentrum Luzern.jpg
File:Aerial view of KKL Luzern with Pilatus.jpg

note: Concert hall opened 1998; whole complex inaugurated 2000.

name: Shelters for the Roman Ruins, Chur
features: Timber-louvred boxes follow the outlines of Roman walls, letting filtered light and air onto the ruins.
note: Only one exterior photo; the rest of the category (12 files) shows the timber-slatted interior over the ruins, which is the point of the building.

name: Zollverein School of Management and Design
features: A concrete cube on the old colliery site, its faces scattered with square windows of many sizes.
award: Pritzker laureate: Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa
note: Category:Zollverein School of Management and Design is empty; the files are in Category:SANAA building at Zollverein Essen. SANAA's works list gives 2003–2006.

name: Burgo Tower
features: Office tower wrapped in a grid of metal bands that reads differently on each face, beside a low block.
award: Pritzker laureate: Eduardo Souto de Moura
note: Named in Souto de Moura's Pritzker citation. Third photo is an artistic view through a sculpture.

name: Meiso no Mori Municipal Funeral Hall
features: Thin white concrete roof that rises and falls like a cloud, resting on tapered columns beside a pond.
note: Crematorium; typed Memorial as for Kaze-no-Oka. Ito's Wikipedia list says 2015, but Architect Magazine gives 2006 and the Commons photos date from 2008.

name: National Stadium, Kaohsiung (World Games Stadium)
features: Open-ended spiral stadium whose roof is covered in solar panels that power most of the building.
note: Second photo is a distant panorama; third is inside the bowl.

name: Swatch Headquarters, Biel
features: A 240 m timber gridshell snakes over the offices, filled with glass, solar and opaque panels.

photos.file: File:Hauptsitz der Swatch AG vom Park aus gesehen.jpg

note: Part of the Swatch and Omega campus; the category also holds the neighbouring Omega buildings, so pick files carefully.

name: Tanzbrunnen (Star Wave Tent)
features: Star-shaped fabric membrane pulled up on masts, floating over a dance floor in a fountain basin.
note: Built for the 1957 Federal Garden Show; the tent itself is Category:Sternwellenzelt (inside Category:Tanzbrunnen, which also covers the later stage).

name: Crematorium Hofheide
features: Long rust-red box of vertical steel fins that seems to float on a pond in open fields.
award: Pritzker laureate: RCR Arquitectes (Aranda, Pigem, Vilalta)
note: Competition won jointly with Coussée & Goris; completed 2014 (Arquitectura Viva gives 2006–2014).

name: Nara Centennial Hall
features: Long hall with curved, dark-tiled walls like a ship's hull, beside Nara station.

photos.file: File:なら100年会館-Nara Centennial Hall(2010-10-11) - panoramio.jpg

note: Main hall seats 1,720 (Wikipedia).

name: Marshall Building, London School of Economics
features: Stone-clad block with deep vertical fins and a cut-open, stepped ground floor drawing in the square.
award: Pritzker laureate: Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara

photos.file: File:The Marshall Building Campus, London School of Economics.jpg

note: Competition won 2016 (Wikipedia); the photos date from March 2022, when it opened. Third photo is 1400px.

name: Opera Village (Operndorf Afrika)
features: Village of school, clinic and houses in local brick and earth, with deep-set windows and shading roofs.
note: Photos are 1633px wide. First two show the school (rendered walls, scattered square windows), the third the houses. Started with Christoph Schlingensief; built in phases from 2010. Wikipedia gives no completion year: 2011 is when the school opened, please double-check.

name: Kunsthaus Zürich Extension
features: Massive rectangular block in pale sandstone with slender vertical fins, facing the old Kunsthaus.
note: Completed 2020, opened to visitors October 2021 (Wikipedia). Only two exterior photos; the second shows it just before completion.

name: West Village (Basis Yard)
features: Five-storey building ringing a whole city block around sports pitches, with a ramp up to the roof.

photos.file: File:成都西村·贝森大院内庭.jpg
File:成都西村·贝森大院全景图.jpg
File:成都西村·贝森大院1号楼.jpg

note: Sources give 2014 or 2015. Second photo is a very wide panorama.

name: Viña Vik Winery
features: Winery set low in the vineyard under a translucent canopy, approached across a shallow water court of stones.
note: Third photo is 1500px. The hotel on the same estate is by Marcelo Daglio, not Radić.

name: Fujisawa Municipal Gymnasium (Akibadai)
features: Two arenas under curved stainless-steel roofs, likened to a samurai helmet or a beetle.
note: No building category; files are in the park's category. File:Fujisawa City Akibadai Gymnasimu 01.jpg (1600px) shows the arena inside.

name: The Circle, Zurich Airport
features: A small city of glass-walled blocks and lanes curving along the hill beside the airport terminal.

photos.file: File:Hyatt Place Zurich Airport The Circle.jpg

note: Weak set: one corner view, one distant view, one entrance. Many construction photos (2017–18) exist. No Commons category found. Offices, hotels, shops and a conference centre.

name: Dominus Winery
features: Long low box walled in gabions of local basalt, which shade the cellars and let light filter through.
note: Only one free photo (portrait format, looking through the central passage). No Commons category. Sources disagree on 1997/1998 and on dimensions.

name: Emerson College Los Angeles
features: Ten-storey frame of two slim residential slabs and a bridge, wrapping a sculpted block of classrooms.
note: Only one free photo (1348 x 1078 px, a street view of the whole building). No Commons category.

name: Vulcania
features: Mostly underground museum marked by a split cone clad in dark volcanic stone and lined with gold.
note: In France (no freedom of panorama; Hollein died 2014), so these could be deleted later. A volcano theme park and museum; three-quarters of it is underground (Wikipedia).

name: Cinémathèque française (former American Center)
features: Stone-clad block whose park side breaks into tilting, folding forms under a curling zinc roof.
note: Weak photos: the first shows the park side partly through trees, the second only the entrance. Paris (no freedom of panorama, Gehry alive), so Commons can't hold a good full view. A drawing would help, but I couldn't establish the facade well enough to draw it accurately. Built 1994 as the American Center; the Cinémathèque moved in 2005.

name: St. Edward's University Residence and Dining Halls
features: Three brick-clad halls for 300 students around a shared inner court, on a narrow campus plot.
note: Hunt, Le Mans and Johnson Halls; Aravena's only US building. No free photo found (the university's Commons category has none of these halls). Its rock-like, faceted massing is too irregular to draw from text alone. Sources give 2008 to 2009.

name: Mahatma Gandhi Labour Institute
features: Academic block along a two-level vaulted spine, with cross-vaults for library and hall, to shade and cool.
note: No free photo on Commons. Sources describe the vaulted spine but not enough of the elevation (vault count, heights, the dormitory tower) to draw it accurately. Built about 1980–84.

name: Cité Manifeste, Mulhouse (14 houses)
features: 14 duplex social homes: a concrete ground floor topped by off-the-shelf horticultural greenhouses.
award: Pritzker laureate: Anne Lacaton and Jean-Philippe Vassal
note: No free photo (France, no freedom of panorama). A good drawing candidate, but sources only say the greenhouse has a 'shallow-arched roof' and don't say which way the arches run or how many there are, so I didn't draw it. One look at a published elevation would settle it.
